controls.reason: Adequate migration support and coexistence depend on complete consumer needs, compatibility behavior and contextual support duration.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Documentation and a dual-version window can exist while an offline consumer cannot migrate and the coexistence period ends too early.

controls.reason: Completeness of consumer inventory and migration evidence cannot be proved by their records, and recovery planning requires operational judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All registered consumers can show migration while an undocumented automation client still uses the deprecated path when it is retired.

controls.reason: Seven default-control labels do not prove least privilege, secure secret use or approved behavior across every generated platform path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A template can contain the expected settings while a generated role is overprivileged or an alternate network path bypasses policy checks.

controls.reason: A role matrix cannot prove control-plane privileges are separated from ordinary teams across every API, emergency path and inherited identity.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Declared roles can be distinct while a shared service account lets an application team perform control-plane changes.

controls.reason: Which actions are high impact and whether they are truly reviewable and auditable require complete action-path coverage beyond record fields.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All registered high-impact actions can have actor and expiry fields while an undocumented admin endpoint remains unattributed.

controls.reason: Preventing five harmful defaults across arbitrary template parameters and generated resources is a security, cost and lifecycle outcome claim.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Standard template tests can pass while a rare parameter combination creates a public resource or unbounded-cost workload.

controls.reason: Validation and safe bounds require a complete parameter inventory plus project-specific resource, region, data, network and identity policies.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known fields can validate while an extension parameter bypasses region restrictions or a configured bound is unsafe for sensitive data.

controls.reason: Five policy-case tests do not prove full rule, parameter, exception, rollback and degraded-path coverage or correct authorization oracles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All named fixtures can pass while an untested exception combination permits a denied production action.

controls.reason: Absence of access to unrelated tenants, teams, environments, repositories and secrets is universal over every automation identity and path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Configured IAM tests can pass while a inherited token or control-plane API exposes another team's production secret.

controls.reason: The platform consumer register cannot prove it contains every nonhuman user, automation, CI identity, service account and AI agent.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All known identities can be present while a vendor bot or dynamically created service account remains unrecorded.

controls.reason: Temporary scoped credential issuance can exist while long-lived shared credentials remain distributed through an unobserved workflow or legacy system.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The approved path passes TTL and scope checks but an old shared deployment key still grants the same platform access.

controls.reason: Each platform-generated configuration, artifact, attestation and audit record can be content-addressed and linked to exact request, policy, source and approver identities.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Any generated item lacking one provenance edge or carrying a mismatched policy digest fails the finite lineage graph.

controls.reason: Break-glass usability during simultaneous identity, documentation and control-plane loss is an empirical resilience property, not a procedure record.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A documented emergency path can pass normal drills while depending indirectly on the failed identity provider.

controls.reason: A versioned service-level policy can define user-facing SLI and SLO records for the seven finite critical workflow classes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: If rollback or secret delivery lacks a user-perspective indicator or objective, the exact seven-workflow join fails.

controls.reason: Consumer-perspective success requires defining complete user tasks and meaningful outcomes; component-uptime plus one synthetic check can falsely pass.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The synthetic environment-creation task can succeed while real consumers consistently fail at a later permission step.

controls.reason: Each registered internal platform service can be required to publish six exact process references for status, incidents, ownership, support, escalation and postmortems.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A service without an escalation path or postmortem process fails the finite service-process schema.

controls.reason: Seven scenario executions do not establish complete platforms, workloads, combinations, timing paths or correctness and recovery oracles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Each named fault can pass alone while throttling during an identity outage deadlocks the queue.

controls.reason: Genuinely critical and supported are contextual classifications, while a passing alternate-path test does not prove operation during real platform loss.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An emergency command can work in staging yet require a production credential issued by the unavailable primary platform.

controls.reason: Guaranteeing outage-time access to runbooks, credentials, artifacts and communication requires exhaustive dependency and correlated-failure coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All four items can have backups while every backup depends on the same unavailable identity or network plane.

controls.reason: A publication registry can require current public entries for maintenance windows, deprecation schedules, breaking changes and reliability limitations.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Omitting any of the four topic records or publishing an unapproved version fails the exact registry.

controls.reason: Rollback and version compatibility across four interface and asset classes are runtime properties over incomplete versions, consumers and state transitions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known combinations can pass while an older generated asset cannot be rolled back after a policy migration.

controls.reason: A platform outcome report can require the seven exact measurements: adoption, failure, support burden, lead time, stability, satisfaction and cost.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A report presenting adoption without user satisfaction or cost fails the finite metric schema; adequacy thresholds are not inferred.

controls.reason: A service-level metric contract can define and compute the five named current DORA outcome signals from versioned event and denominator rules.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Omitting deployment rework rate or using an unapproved denominator fails the exact five-metric contract.

controls.reason: Delivery events and denominators can be versioned with effective periods so comparisons require the same definitions or explicit normalization.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A trend crossing a silent denominator change fails the metric-version compatibility check.

controls.reason: Every published delivery metric can be required to include seven exact metadata fields covering definition, source, exclusions, bias, confidence and decision use.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A metric without known-bias or intended-decision metadata fails the schema.

controls.reason: Audit occurrence across six bias labels does not prove gaming, missing work or changed process semantics were correctly detected.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All checklist sections can be complete while teams reclassify failed deployments in a way the audit does not recognize.

controls.reason: Preference, vanity and appropriate use of trends or distributions are interpretive reporting choices rather than objective record states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A report can include a distribution yet emphasize a misleading isolated average as the decision signal.

controls.reason: An intervention record can require the five exact predeclared elements: baseline, mechanism, counter-metrics, observation period and rollback criteria.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An intervention launched without a baseline or with rollback criteria added afterward fails the finite schema and timestamp rule.

controls.reason: Every policy-tagged material investment can be checked for the eight exact decision, alternatives, objectives, constraints, stakeholders, horizon and owner fields.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An investment lacking alternatives or a decision owner cannot pass the structured business-case record.

controls.reason: Whether a point estimate is unjustifiably precise and which ranges and scenarios are decision-relevant require estimation judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A model can show a narrow range and two nominal scenarios while hiding the major supplier-risk uncertainty.

controls.reason: Materiality of present-value analysis and the correct discount treatment require economic, horizon and policy judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A consistent discount formula can pass while using an inappropriate rate or omitting a material long-term benefit.

controls.reason: Correctly distinguishing sunk from future decision-relevant costs requires economic interpretation of obligations and alternatives.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every cost row can have a category while a cancelable future commitment is incorrectly labeled sunk.

controls.reason: Complete identification of irreversible commitments, lock-in and switching costs plus valuation of options requires open-ended commercial judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All four sections can be populated while a proprietary data-format lock-in or valuable delay option is omitted.

controls.reason: Expected loss across eight risk domains requires uncertain probability, consequence and legal estimates from specialist evidence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All eight values can be present while privacy or supplier loss is severely understated under an invalid model.

controls.reason: Sensitivity execution is bounded, but choosing the assumption space and interpreting which assumptions dominate the real decision is contextual.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A model can show one dominant parameter while omitting the uncertainty that actually changes the preferred option.

controls.reason: An investment gate can require defined leading indicators and exact stop, pivot, expand and review thresholds before full commitment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A threshold missing or timestamped after commitment fails the finite precommitment policy record.

controls.reason: Links to five actual evidence types do not prove all costs, benefits, adoption, quality and risks are correct or complete after delivery.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The case can update each section while omitting indirect support cost and an emerging security risk.

controls.reason: Every uncertainty and residual-risk entry can require the accepting identity, authority, timestamp and explicit acceptance event.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A risk hidden only inside an estimate or lacking an accountable acceptor fails the ledger join.

controls.reason: An estimate can be checked for the eight exact purpose, scope, date, confidence, currency, price-basis and lifecycle-stage fields.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing confidence needs or lifecycle stages creates a deterministic estimate-schema failure.

controls.reason: Actual reproducibility and reviewer qualification require human competence plus an executable, complete calculation model, not documentation presence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A seemingly detailed estimate can omit an implicit spreadsheet adjustment so another qualified estimator cannot reproduce it.

controls.reason: Milestone alignment and numeric variance are bounded, but explaining variance by its true cause requires causal business and delivery judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The report can compare every milestone and assign causes while blaming staffing rather than the actual supplier delay.

controls.reason: Materiality and complete detection of seven change types are contextual and unbounded, so re-estimation triggers can miss real changes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Configured changes can trigger estimates while an indirect architecture change is missed or a quality change is deemed immaterial.

controls.reason: An estimate state machine can forbid commitment from exploratory status unless new evidence is linked and confidence classification explicitly changes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A direct exploratory-to-committed transition with unchanged confidence or no new evidence fails the exact gate.

controls.reason: All material work and external dependencies cannot be proven complete from the delivery model, and materiality is contextual.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every named category can have tasks while an approval, migration or retirement activity remains undiscovered.

controls.reason: A delivery model can require explicit dependency edges and task-logic fields and prohibit independent free-standing date commitments.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A task date with no duration, predecessor or scheduling rule fails the finite graph schema.

controls.reason: The critical path is computable, but near-critical lacks a stated threshold and complete task/dependency discovery is unbounded.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The schedule can monitor computed paths while an omitted supplier dependency is actually critical or the near-critical cutoff is arbitrary.

controls.reason: A delivery resource model can require the seven exact availability, skill, leave, support, review, environment and supplier-lead-time dimensions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A schedule model without review capacity or supplier lead times fails the finite model schema; forecast accuracy is not inferred.

controls.reason: A work-flow ledger can compute the five exact blocked, queue, rework, dependency-age and decision-latency durations from state timestamps.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing transition time or one required measure fails the finite metric calculation.

controls.reason: Milestone completion can require linked verifiable outcome and evidence identities and reject percentage-complete as the sole criterion.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A milestone marked complete at ninety percent with no outcome evidence fails the state-transition guard.

controls.reason: A reforecast can be bound to observed throughput and discovered-work snapshots and supersede rather than preserve the prior obsolete date.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A forecast copied from the old date without current input identities fails provenance and supersession checks.

controls.reason: Adequate observation time is contextual and depends on risk, traffic cycles and failure latency despite five window fields being present.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All five windows can be defined while stabilization ends before a monthly workload or delayed migration failure appears.

controls.reason: Every committed scope or schedule change can require an append-only decision-log entry with reason, actor, time and affected baseline.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A changed committed date without a linked decision event fails the baseline-diff join.

controls.reason: A selection gate can require versioned capability and quality requirements dated before any product, provider, framework or sourcing choice.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A provider selected before the requirement-set timestamp or with no quality requirements fails the temporal gate.

controls.reason: Where risk warrants and complete discovery of sub-suppliers and external dependencies require risk judgment and supply-chain inventory completeness.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known high-risk suppliers can be listed while a critical fourth party remains hidden or wrongly rated low risk.

controls.reason: A procurement evidence package can require linked evidence for the eight exact security, accessibility, compliance, location, deletion, backup, notification and continuity claims.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A selected supplier claim without accessibility or deletion evidence fails the finite evidence matrix.

controls.reason: Representative proof and complete integration and migration costs require workload, architecture and economic judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A pilot can use a nominal sample while excluding the hardest data migration and production authentication integration.

controls.reason: Actual user objectives, adequate service-level tests and contract remedies require empirical outcome evidence plus legal and business judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A synthetic SLA test can pass while the contractual target misses a critical user journey and remedies are unenforceable.

controls.reason: Whether contracts retain enforceable rights to six data and artifact classes is a legal interpretation, not a clause-presence fact.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All six nouns can appear while provider exceptions prevent export of necessary logs at termination.

controls.reason: A precommitment exit plan can be checked for seven exact termination, assistance, revocation, return, deletion, transition and cost definitions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A commitment without credential-revocation or exit-cost terms fails the finite plan schema.

controls.reason: A code-ownership policy can define accountable owners for forks, patches, vendored code, unsupported versions and upstream contributions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Any of the five code states without an owner fails the exact mapping.

controls.reason: Continuous detection of supplier changes across seven effects requires complete supplier inventory and external price, terms and product feeds.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Configured alerts can all be current while a supplier silently changes data use or regional availability.

controls.reason: A ten-area capability map cannot prove actual human knowledge, skill depth, coverage or correctness of self-reported capabilities.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All areas can have named people and ratings while no one can operate a critical recovery procedure.

controls.reason: Critical-service completeness and qualified-person status require human competence judgment, while accessible documentation does not prove operational ability.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Two people can be listed with documentation access while neither can execute the recovery procedure during an incident.

controls.reason: Planning occurrence is visible, but whether training is adequate before teams operate technology safely requires competence and safety judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A short recorded course can precede launch while operators remain unable to handle a dangerous failure mode.

controls.reason: A workforce transition plan can require the five exact succession, offboarding, access-removal, artifact-transfer and ownership-reassignment procedures.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Omitting artifact transfer or access removal fails the finite plan schema.

controls.reason: A critical-capability acquisition gate can require accountable owner, operating model, support plan and retirement path before buy or build approval.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Any critical capability missing one of the four records cannot pass the exact no-go gate.

controls.reason: Consumer inventory completeness, compatibility evidence and recovery effectiveness cannot be proved by records before forced migration.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All known consumers can receive communication while an offline supported client remains incompatible and unrecoverable.

controls.reason: Each registered internal engineering capability can be required to define users, outcomes, owners, roadmap, support and lifecycle decisions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A capability without identifiable users or retirement decision policy fails the six-field product schema.

controls.reason: A platform persona policy can define the seven finite developer, operator, analyst, data, security, support and partner personas.
controls.counterexample_analysis: If partner or support users lack a defined persona, the exact seven-class schema fails.

controls.reason: A platform strategy can explicitly define its target outcome set and bind each outcome to a versioned indicator identity.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A strategy with no safe-delivery or feedback outcome definition fails its declared outcome schema; improvement is not inferred.

controls.reason: Every platform control can be classified mandatory or optional, and each mandatory control can require an explicit rationale.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unclassified control or mandatory control without a reason fails the finite policy registry.

controls.reason: A responsibility matrix can assign each registered platform boundary to exactly one of platform, product-team or supplier ownership.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A responsibility with no owner or conflicting direct owners fails the finite three-party mapping.

controls.reason: A published platform-service record can require five exact boundary, use-case, non-goal, dependency and escalation sections.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A service with no non-goals or escalation model fails the finite publication schema.

controls.reason: A searchable catalog with eleven fields cannot prove inclusion of every real service, pipeline, environment and dependency.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All entries can be complete while a shadow application or unregistered data pipeline remains absent.

controls.reason: Assigning owner and contact to every production component requires a complete production-component inventory not proven by the catalog.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every catalog entry can have both fields while an undocumented production job remains unowned.

controls.reason: Each catalog entry can be validated for the ten exact repository, documentation, operations, SLO, data, API, dependency and deployment fields.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An entry missing data classification or deployment location fails the finite catalog schema.

controls.reason: Orphaned, duplicate, abandoned, unsupported and unowned status requires complete component discovery plus semantic lifecycle and equivalence judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known entries can be classified while a duplicate shadow service remains undiscovered or an active component is wrongly marked abandoned.

controls.reason: Reliable automation and metadata staleness require source-specific judgment, thresholds and complete synchronization-path coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A sync job can be marked reliable while silently dropping owners, and manual metadata can pass review just before becoming stale.

controls.reason: Catalog metadata can carry an exact authority type distinguishing authoritative values from discovered and inferred values with source provenance.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An inferred owner labeled authoritative or an untyped field violates the finite metadata schema.

controls.reason: Useful relationship exposure and absence of sensitive topology leakage require authorization semantics and complete response and query-path coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Authorized users can view known dependencies while an unauthenticated search or error response leaks a restricted network relationship.

controls.reason: Integration records do not prove incident, vulnerability, deprecation and cost events are routed correctly across all ownership changes and failure paths.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All four connectors can exist while stale ownership sends a critical vulnerability notice to the wrong team.

controls.reason: Defined registration and retirement workflows cannot prove that every creation and deletion path is forced through inventory.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The official workflow can update the catalog while a direct infrastructure API creates a component without registration.

controls.reason: Catalog entity identities can be immutable and aliases can map renames, moves and platform migrations back to the same identifier.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Issuing a new identity during a rename or losing the migration alias fails the exact identity-continuity check.

controls.reason: Catalog coverage cannot be known without a complete external inventory, and freshness requires source-specific thresholds and semantics.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The dashboard can show full coverage of registered sources while a shadow service is absent and stale owner data appears current.

controls.reason: Availability of emergency contacts during correlated catalog and identity failure is an empirical recovery property, not a backup-record fact.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An offline contact file can exist but be encrypted with a key available only through the failed identity platform.

controls.reason: Secure, observable, supportable and maintained defaults are platform-quality and lifecycle judgments across incomplete common workflows.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A recommended template can be documented and instrumented while its default role is overprivileged or dependency abandoned.

controls.reason: Each registered recommended path can be content-versioned, linked to documentation and tests, and reproduced from pinned inputs and artifacts.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A path with mutable inputs, no test identity or a replay digest mismatch fails the bounded provenance contract.

controls.reason: Every generated project manifest can require owner, dependency provenance, update path, test references and removal instructions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A project missing dependency lineage or removal instructions fails the finite five-field generation schema.

controls.reason: Current standards require changing external and internal authority, while continuous test occurrence does not prove examples behave correctly.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Examples can run on every commit while still teach an obsolete security pattern or assert the wrong output.

controls.reason: Clear support, compatibility and change models are qualitative and do not prove actual maintenance or compatibility across consumers.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All three documents can exist while the shared library silently breaks an older supported client.

controls.reason: Legitimacy of exceptions, reviewer quality and adequate risk treatment require accountable security and product judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every escape hatch can have approval and owner fields while an unjustified exception removes a critical control.

controls.reason: Guaranteeing escape paths do not silently remove five quality controls requires complete generated configurations and runtime path coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The standard exception test can pass while one escape option disables audit logging or accessibility behavior.

controls.reason: Each registered recommended path can be required to report five exact adoption, abandonment, support, defect and satisfaction measures.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A path missing support burden or user satisfaction data fails the finite metric schema; metric quality is not inferred.

controls.reason: Migration tooling and communication are observable, but sufficient support windows depend on consumer risk, usage cycles and migration complexity.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A deprecated path can have all three records while the window ends before a dormant supported consumer can migrate.

controls.reason: Inspection access can be provided, but whether teams understand generated configuration and infrastructure is a human comprehension outcome.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Configuration can be visible and documented while users misunderstand a generated privilege or network rule.

controls.reason: Absence of secrets, obsolete dependencies, insecure defaults and organization identifiers is an open-world negative security claim across generated output.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Scans can pass while an encoded secret or transitive obsolete dependency remains in one generated variant.

controls.reason: Low-risk classification requires judgment, and working self-service access across all authorized users and actions is an operational behavior claim.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The catalog can label actions low risk and ticketless while one action is actually high impact or fails for an authorized role.

controls.reason: Determining which policies are deterministic and which decisions require human approval, exceptions or high-impact risk judgment is itself contextual governance work.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A rule can be wrongly automated despite needing interpretation, while a subjective low-impact request is needlessly sent to humans.

controls.reason: Clarity of inputs, previews and consequences plus adequacy of validation and cost implications require user and domain judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All five UI sections can exist while the preview hides a destructive consequence or cost estimate misleads users.

controls.reason: Idempotence and safe retry are runtime semantic properties across every workflow state, side effect, failure and timing path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known retry tests can pass while a timeout after commit causes a duplicate resource or repeated charge.
